text:
ana: Deploybot raised an anomaly during v4.0.0 rollout in us-east. autopilot proposed rollback but was blocked by a config mismatch. Can we decide manual vs rapid rollforward?

mike: seeing p95 jump +350ms on long-context generator in us-east canary (slice 4%). no user 5xxs, requests succeed slower.

ops-bot: snapshot: region=use1 canary=4% p95_delta=+350ms error_rate=0.4% baseline=0.6% host_restarts=0

tara: autopilot blocked because rollout config had "require-operator=true" for core models. that's intentional. we need operator handshake to proceed.

ana: typo: that's me, "ana". mike, are we confident this is model-side not infra?

mike: reproduced on staging with long-history prompts. points at scheduler heuristics in v4.0.0. infra looks green.

legal-bot: advise avoiding saying "rollback" in external comms. prefer "restored previous stable release" wording.

support: can we get a one-line for support triage if we revert? customers asking in tickets.

ana: if we revert, comms: "Restored stable v3.9.8 in affected region due to observed latency increase in a canary slice; investigating". tara you OK to own the release-note line?

tara: i will. also recommend operator-lock so autopilot won't try to reapply v4.0.0 while we debug.

mike: two options: (A) manual rollback to v3.9.8 now, or (B) quick hotfix flip to disable new scheduler heuristics in v4.0.0 and rollforward. hotfix will need build + smoke tests ~25-40m. rollback is fast.

ana: ops prefer rollback for speed. leads: who's operator to execute? we need handshake to satisfy deploy config.

mike: i can be operator but i'm on-call for infra too. jamming both is meh. @tara?

tara: i can do operator. execute command: `/deploy revert --to v3.9.8 --operator tara --operator-lock reason="canary latency"`

deploybot: Request received. validating operator-lock and prechecks...

deploybot: Prechecks OK  artifact v3.9.8 found, migrations none, operator-lock token granted. Initiating revert: remove canary of v4.0.0 -> restore v3.9.8. ETA ~3m.

ops-bot: starting traffic shift now. monitoring p95, qps.

deploybot: Revert complete. state: active=v3.9.8 inactive=v4.0.0 canary=0% operator-lock=true

mike: confirmed p95 back to baseline within 90s. opening REL-7001 to track scheduler heuristic regression and hotfix plan.

support: shared short blurb to affected customers and updated incident ticket. thanks.

legal-bot: reviewed comms draft; remove any mention of "incident severity" in external line.

tara: release notes line added: "Temporarily restored v3.9.8 in us-east due to observed latency with v4.0.0 canary; follow-up patch planned."

ana: next steps: owners mike+tara to debug and test hotfix, ops to monitor for 24h with operator-lock in place, support to notify customers if tickets escalate. closing thread unless new signals show up. :white_check_mark:
